question: If $k$ is an integer such that $\lim_{n\to\infty}\left[\left(\cos\frac{k\pi}{4}\right)^n-\left(\cos\frac{k\pi}{6}\right)^n\right]=0$, then

options.A: $k$ is divisible neither by 4 nor by 6
options.B: $k$ must be divisible by 12, but not necessarily by 24
options.D: either $k$ is divisible by 24 or $k$ is divisible neither by 4 nor by 6

source.title: Test of Mathematics at the 10+2 Level
